description: Canal-belt cornice house under a Louis XIV attic (Keizersgracht 244-246, twin fronts): a 6-7 m front of ochre brick, a tall ground storey at street level (door in a white pilaster surround and tall windows) and three upper storeys of three axes of white-framed six-pane windows with white sills, under a white attic band over the cornice with one dark light per axis and a carved crest

match.note: Keizersgracht 244 (169108) and 246 (169380), 2021-01-22 strip at 40 px/m, gridded: ground openings 1.8-5.0 m, rows 6.0-8.6, 9.0-11.4, 12.0-13.8 m, cornice foot 14.9 m, attic lights 15.5-16.2 m, attic top 17.3 m, crest to 18.3 m. Placed only by a reviewer's pand pin

louis.note: Keizersgracht 246 (169380), 2021-01-22 strip gridded at 2x (grid-crop 2950-3190): a white attic 14.2-17.0 m with three lights 15.0-15.9 m, then a Louis XIV crest across the front, C-scrolls and short balustrades at both ends about 1 m high, a raised central arch to 19.2 m and a carved top to 19.6 m

door-left.note: the house door at street level on the outer axis (246 left, 244 right: a mirrored pair)

rhythm.bays: 3 axes (4 over 7.6 m, 5 over 9.8 m: the double-wide Herengracht fronts)
rhythm.groundFloor: door in a white pilaster surround and tall windows at street level
rhythm.roofline: a white attic band with a light per axis under a carved crest
schemaLimits: the crest is drawn as the small kit crest: the real one is a carved Louis XIV attic spanning the front with an oculus
the white pilaster door surround is drawn as a plain door with a transom
